architecture.approach: Add three Markdown documents under docs/design-partners/ and link them from the README. The program page defines eligibility, obligations, the production definition, and the G5 gate; the tracker is an empty template with fixed columns and no invented partner; the case-study template carries consent, a redaction checklist, and measured outcomes. A small Node check validates the required sections and that no placeholder row claims a partner.

components.name: docs/design-partners/program.md
components.description: Eligibility, benefits, obligations, production definition, G5 gate.

components.name: docs/design-partners/tracker.md
components.description: Empty template with seven columns; no fabricated partner.

components.name: scripts/docs-partners.js
components.description: Validates required sections, tracker columns, placeholders, and the evidence-link rule.

dataModel.flowDescription: The maintainer adds a tracker row only after a partner consents, records an evidence link, and sets status to prospect, active, case study published, or declined. A case study is drafted from the template, redacted against the checklist, and published only with written approval. There is no runtime data and no storage.

securityConsiderations.description: Documents use placeholders such as <project-name> and follow the repository writing conventions.
Pages are plain Markdown rendered by GitHub; no build step and no executable content.

performanceConsiderations.strategy: A Markdown table is the source of truth; the checker is one linear pass over three small files.

risks.description: Adoption is external and may not materialise.
risks.mitigation: The feature makes the requirement visible and auditable, not guaranteed.

risks.description: A thin documentation feature can become a filing exercise.
risks.mitigation: The empty-template and sourcing rules keep it honest.
The tracker records roles rather than people and the template mandates redaction.
